text:
NEW YORK, Sept 10 (Reuters) - My social feeds are filled with photos of kids heading off to college. A big question among my mom friends is: How much spending money do they need?
To figure out the right amount (and launch financially responsible adults in ​the process), here are three essential action items: make a budget, create a spending plan and build an ‌emergency fund.
And since many kids are getting credit cards for the first time, I got advice on that topic, too.
After you read and share my article on this topic, let me know how you’re handling college spending! If you have any other thoughts/tips, please email me via the link in my ​bio.
Full disclosure: I deleted the section on working in college because my article was getting too long — but I’m ​a big fan of having a job for extra cash and using some of that money to ⁠start saving for retirement!

"Your career is not a ladder. It’s a jungle gym," according to Sarah Franklin, chief executive officer at Lattice, the people management platform.
Her trajectory up the corporate ladder — from a sales clerk to debugging German code at a major consulting firm to chief marketing officer at Salesforce to her current role as CEO — was filled with unexpected twists, turns and a few memorable spills.
I ​love talking to people about ​their first jobs for Reuters. (I ⁠publish these interviews in tandem with the U.S. employment report.)
